NA

Source: manual_cran_comments.md

  • This patch release addresses the two problems that CRAN’s clang sanitizer checks reported in third-party compiled code reached from artma’s test suite. There are no reverse dependencies.

  • The clang-ASAN failure reported on 2026-10-13 was a memcpy-param-overlap in agg::font_cache_pool::font() (agg_font_cache_manager.h:176), which is part of ‘ragg’, not artma’s own compiled code. ragg 1.5.2 evicts the oldest entry of its process-wide font cache with an overlapping memcpy() once more than 32 font configurations have been drawn, and a test worker that exports many plots goes past that limit. The test suite now renders PNG exports with grDevices::png() instead of ‘ragg’. ‘ragg’ stays in Suggests and is still preferred for exports outside the tests.

  • The clang-san pre-test of the 0.5.1 submission then reported call to function clear_console through pointer to incorrect function type 'void (*)(struct SEXPREC *)' at memory.c:1524. That function belongs to ‘rjags’ (src/jags.cc), which registers SEXP clear_console(SEXP) as a void (*)(SEXP) C finalizer for its JAGS console pointer; the function-type sanitizer flags the mismatch when R runs the finalizer. The one test that fits a ‘RoBMA’ model, and so loads ‘rjags’ into the test process, is now skipped on CRAN and still runs in the package’s own continuous integration. No artma code changed for this.
